items.prompt: White plays 1.Rac1, putting a rook on the half-open c-file. Is Black's c6 pawn now a fixed target under attack? It is fixed only if the square in front of it, c5, is attacked by a White pawn. Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Black's c6 pawn is backward.
One White pawn (d4) attacks c5, the square in front of the c6 pawn.
After Rac1 the rook attacks c6.
Rac1 and Rfc1 are the engine's top two moves.

hints: Two things must both be true: the rook attacks the pawn, and the pawn cannot step forward safely.
Look at c5 and at the c-file between the rook and the c6 pawn.
Is c5 attacked by a pawn? Is anything of White's own standing on the c-file in the way?
items.explain: c6 is backward (the d4 pawn attacks c5, so the pawn cannot advance safely) and Rac1 puts a rook on the half-open file against it. The engine's two best moves are the two rook moves to the c-file.

items.prompt: White plays 1.Rac1, putting a rook on the half-open c-file. Is Black's c6 pawn now a fixed target under attack? It is fixed only if the square in front of it, c5, is attacked by a White pawn. Predict, then check.

items.explain: The rook does attack c6, but no White pawn attacks c5, so the pawn is not backward: it can step forward to c5. The target is not fixed. (Whether Black should step forward is a separate question; only the stop-square fact is claimed.)

items.prompt: White to move. 1.b4 attacks the knight on a5. Does it win the knight? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: After b4 the knight on a5 has two legal moves (b3 and c4).
1.b4 wins at least a knight for a pawn along the engine's line.

hints: Do not ask whether the knight is attacked. Ask where it can go.
List the squares the knight can reach after b4, and who covers each.
Count the knight's escape squares: a piece that has none is a target even though it can move.
items.explain: After b4 the knight has only two legal moves, b3 and c4, and the engine's line wins it. The kick pays here because the piece has no safe retreat.

items.prompt: Black to move. d5 is a hole in White's camp: no White pawn can ever attack it. Black plays ...Nd5. Can White challenge the knight there, by attacking d5 with a pawn or a piece? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: d5 is a hole in White's camp.
No White pawn attacks d5.
No White piece attacks d5 after ...Nd5.

hints: A hole only helps if the piece that lands on it can stay.
Look at every White piece and ask which squares it attacks.
Does any White piece attack d5 after the knight arrives?
items.explain: d5 is a hole, and after ...Nd5 neither a White pawn nor a White piece attacks the knight, so the hole is usable.

items.prompt: Black to move. d5 is a hole in White's camp: no White pawn can ever attack it. Black plays ...Nd5. Can White challenge the knight there, by attacking d5 with a pawn or a piece? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: d5 is still a hole in White's camp.
No White pawn attacks d5.
One White piece (the knight on c3) attacks d5 after ...Nd5.

hints: A hole only helps if the piece that lands on it can stay.

items.explain: The hole is the same, but the knight on c3 attacks d5, so White can challenge the knight on the very square the hole was meant to give Black (Nxd5 offers a trade). The hole gives Black less here; the engine still rates ...Nd5 as one of Black's best moves, so this is a weaker hole, not a worthless one.
